In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Erica Macpherson Editor - Paul Duke Director - Calum Angus Mackay Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: Surfing: Marcachd an Tuinn/Riding the Wave
programme.desc:
Aig Geamannan Oilimpigeach 2024, tha an luchd-surfaidh as fheàrr san t-saoghal gu bhith a’ farpais 20,000 cileameatair air falbh bho Paris, ann an Tahiti. Tha tè aig a bheil ùidh mhòr ann an surfadh, Ceitlin Lilidh a’ toirt thugainn sreath de dhà phàirt air eachdraidh surfadh air feadh an t-saoghail. Do mhuinntir Tahiti, far an do thòisich surfadh bho thùs, tha e nas motha na spòrs, ’s e taisbeanadh a th’ ann de chultar mhuinntir an uisge, muinntir Pholinìsia.
Le tòrr de chultar agus eachdraidh bheairteach muinntir Pholinìsia cha mhòr air a sguabhadh air falbh, feumar taing a thoirt do leithid Tom Pōhaku Stone oir chaidh traidiseanan a bhith a’ dannsa air bùird fiodha a thoirt chun an ath ghinealaich agus chun an t-saoghail air fad, far a bheil a-nis, na deichean de mhilleanan dhaoine le ùidh ann an surfadh. Airson a’ chiad uair, tha àite aig surfadh aig na Geamannan Oilimpigeach.
Bho bhith na chur-seachad annasach do luchd-turais bhon Taobh an Iar a’ dol a Hawaii tràth anns an fhicheadamh linn gu bhith na phàirt mhòr de dhòigh-beatha na tràghad ann an California air taobh an iar Ameireagaidh. Cha tug e fada gus an do ràinig surfadh cladaichean fuar na h-Alba is dithis no triùir a’ cur aodach snàmh orra agus a’ dol a-mach air na bùird aca fhèin.
Bho stuadhan mòra Tahiti gu dùbhlain nan tonn sa gheamhradh ann an Inbhir Theòrsa agus tachartasan stuadhan mòra Nazaré ann am Portugal. ’S e sgeulachd de spioradalachd, spòrs, daoine ainmeil, fasan agus fealla-dhà a th’ ann an cuairt Ceitlin Lilidh ’s i ag ionnsachadh mu eachdraidh surfadh.
At the 2024 Olympic Games, the world's best surfers competed 20,000km from Paris, in Tahiti. Keen surfer Ceitlin Lilidh presents a series on the world history of surfing. Much more than a sport to the people of Tahiti where surfing was born, it is an expression of a culture, the people of the water, the Polynesians.
While much of the rich culture and history of the Polynesian people was almost wiped out, thanks to guardians like Tom Pōhaku Stone, the traditions of dancing on wooden boards was passed on to future generations and to the rest of the world - where it is now practised by tens of millions of enthusiasts. Surfing has now for the first time earned its place at the Olympics.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc:
’S caomh leinn a bhith smaoineachadh gu bheil eòlas againn air an t-saoghal timcheall oirnn, ach dè ma tha sinn dìreach a’ faicinn pàirt dheth? Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ toirt cuireadh dhuinn coiseachd, snàmh agus leum am measg nam beathaichean agus an saoghal aca a thuigsinn nan àrainneachd fhèin.
Thairis air ceithir eapasodan iongantach, tha sinn ag ionnsachadh mu chiad-fàthan cumhachdach nam beathaichean, bho fradharc buileach mionaideach gu iasg a tha a’ blasad len craiceann. Faic mar a tha tìgearan gan cleith fhèin le bhith a’ cleachdadh an dath orains, mar a tha leumadairean a’ seòladh a’ chuain le echo-location, mathain-nighe a’ dèanamh an slighe le spògan air leth faireachail, agus tha fiù ’s craobhan a’ cur a-mach rabhaidhean ceimigeach.
Tha Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean a’ taisbeanadh taobhan falaichte de nàdar - cailèideascop de chiad-fàthan nach eil sinn ach air tòiseachadh a’ tuigsinn.
We like to think we know the world around us, but what if we’re only seeing part of the picture? Wild Senses invites you to walk, swim or leap in someone else’s paws, fins or wings - and experience life from a wild perspective.
Across four mind-blowing episodes, we uncover animal supersenses, from high-resolution vision to fish that taste with their skin. Discover how tigers turn orange into camouflage, dolphins navigate the deep using echolocation, raccoons feel their way with hyper-sensitive paws, and even trees send out chemical alarms. The series reveals the hidden side of nature - a kaleidoscope of sensations we’re only just beginning to understand.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na ciad ceumannan a tha a dhìth airson ar misneachadh gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Thairis air an t-sreath, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas mu charaidean, an dachaigh, an teaghlach, obair agus an aimsir am measg gu leòr eile ann an dòigh a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir ann an dramathan goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn luchd-ionnsachaidh èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr agus cuid a bha fileanta agus a sguir ga cleachdadh, agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba is e ann an diofar àitichean air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne: www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan a tha ri fhaighinn air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the first steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she’ll introduce words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy will support us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, family, home, work and weather.
We meet diligent learners who have embraced speaking Gaelic, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. The intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Executive Producer - Una McDonald Producer - Colin MacLeod.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc:
Seo an fharpais-cheist far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Le Niall Iain Dòmnhallach aig an stiùir cluichidh na sgiobaidhean anns an stiùideo an aghaidh an ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a tha a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin agus a tha a’ cur nan ceistean. A’ strì an aghaidh na Mas Fhìoraich airson feuchainn air an duais mhòr, tha DK is Kenna agus Kirsty is Seònaid.
Presented by Niall Iain MacDonald, this is the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Playing from the comfort of their own homes are the Pretenders, and they are the ones posing the questions. Battling the Pretenders to win the big prize are DK and Kenna, and Kirsty and Janet.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Dha cuid de bhoireannaich, ’s urrainn dhan chuairt aca a bhith a’ tachairt gu h-àbhaisteach, ach do chuid eile, chan eil e cho furasta agus bidh tinneasan sònraichte a’ dèanamh cron orra. Bhon fheadhainn a bhios a’ dèiligeadh ri Sionndram Ioma-Ghucach nan Ughagan (SIGU) chun a’ Chràidh, tha sinn a’ faighinn a-mach ciamar a tha an t-àm dhen mhìos a’ toirt buaidh air am beatha làitheil. Tha sinn cuideachd a’ coinneachadh ri na h-eòlaichean, an t-Ollamh Colin Duncan agus an t-Ollamh Andrew Horne bhon Ionad airson Slàinte Ghineamhainn gus tuigse agus mìneachadh a thoirt dhuinn air na tinneasan seo.
Tha sinn a’ coinneachadh ri na peathraichean, Claire agus Emma NicLeòid à Scalpaigh, air a bheil SIGU ach aig a bheil siomptaman gu tur eadar-dhealaichte. Ciamar a tha cùisean air atharrachadh dhaibhsan thar nam bliadhnaichean agus ciamar a tha e a’ toirt buaidh air am beatha bho là gu là?
An dèidh trì bliadhna as aonais sileadh mìos, roghnaich Màiri NicLeòid à Leòdhas, tè eile air a bheil SIGU, an dòigh-beatha aice atharrachadh a chiallaich gun thòisich an cuairt aice a-rithist. Airson Màiri, tha seo a’ ciallachadh dòchas às ùr gun urrainn dhi fhèin agus an duine aice teaghlach a thòiseachadh is iad a-nis a’ coimhead ri slighe tro IVF.
Tha tòrr còmhraidh ann an-dràsta mu dheidhinn fuil-mìos agus spòrs. Leis an sin, tha sinn a’ bruidhinn ris an luth-chleasaiche ainmeil, Eilish McColgan gus faighinn a-mach mar a tha an t-àm dhen mhìos air buaidh a thoirt air a beatha fhèin agus air a dreuchd agus tha sinn cuideachd a’ coimhead ri na stuthan a th’ air a’ mhargaidh ceangailte ri fuil-mìos a’ sealltainn gu bheil na làithean de chriosan mìosail seachad le taghadh nas fharsainge a-nis aig boireannaich.
For some women a period is a normal monthly occurrence but for others, it’s not as straightforward and they may be affected by conditions that impact their menstrual cycle. From those dealing with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) to endometriosis, we find out how symptoms encroach on their daily lives. We talk to experts Professor Colin Duncan and Professor Andrew Horne from the Centre for Reproductive Health, to help us understand what each of these conditions mean.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.sub-title: Fuaim an Airgid – The Sound of Cash ║ S1E3/6
programme.desc:
After years of unhappiness, mill worker Mairead finally walks out of her decades-long marriage and into the arms of the person she loves - hotel owner Cairistiona. However, as the women agree to wait for the right time to tell Mairead’s husband Boyd they are together, little do they know there’s someone watching from the shadows.
Às dèidh bliadhnaichean de mhì-thoileachas, tha neach-obrach na muilne, Mairead, a’ fàgail an duine aice às dèidh bliadhnaichean fada pòsta airson a bhith còmhla ris an neach air a bheil gaol aice – Cairistìona, aig a bheil an taigh-òsta. Ach, ged a tha na boireannaich agaontachadh feitheamh gus innse dha Boyd, an duine aig Mairead, gu bheil iad còmhla – ‘s beag a dh’fhios a th’ aca gu bheil cuideigin ‘san dorchadas gan coimhead.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Seumas - Ewen MacKinnon Sileas - Erica Morrison Donald - Eoghan MacDonald Murdina - Emma MacLeod Cairistiona - Kathryn MacKay Boyd - David Walker Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Production Manager - Mairi MacKinnon.

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc:
Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus ionnsachadh mun sgaradh mòr eadar beartas agus bochdainn ann an São Paulo, Braisil. Bho na coimhearsnachdan beartach glaiste air cùl gheataichean tèarainteachd gu na favelas a tha a’ cuir thairis le sluagh, tha ballachan do-fhaicsinneach a’ sgaradh dhaoine bho chèile sa bhaile seo. Air an turas aige, cluinnidh Ramsay bho dhaoine a tha feuchainn ris an sgaradh seo a thoirt às a chèile le bhith a’ cruthachadh chothroman do dhaoine ann an cuid de na coimhearsnachdan far a bheil an ana-chothrom as motha ri fhaicinn.
Ramsay MacMahon goes on a journey to find out about the deep divide between wealth and poverty in São Paulo, Brazil. From the affluent gated communities to the overcrowded favelas, invisible walls separate people in this city. On his journey, Ramsay hears from individuals who are determined to break down division by creating opportunities for people within some of the city's most disadvantaged communities.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc:
Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh.
The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s-1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Narrator - Kirsty Macdonald Producer - Andy Mackinnon Production Manager - Eilidh Johnson Executive Producer - Margaret Cameron.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc:
A mockumentary shadowing a company that services short term lets. Angela and Katie aim to clean-up and give the competition a bleaching. Blockages need to be dealt with, not just unclogging hot tub filters. A new staff member has a few skeletons in his cupboard but ex-con Daniel hopes he has a squeaky-clean future.
Meanwhile, Betty meets Daniel’s pregnant partner Dido and checks in on her beloved pet pooch Buster. Soon the police are knocking on the company’s portacabin door. Written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan. Angela - Lana Pheutan Katie - Hannah McKirdy Seonaidh - Iain Beggs Daniel - Calum Macdonald Dido - Mairead Hamilton Director - Fiann Macleod.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc:
Nuair tha ruitheam a’ chiùil bhon rèidio a’ còrdadh ri Boban cho mòr ‘s gu bheil e toirt air danns', chan eil Fuigheag buileach a' tuigs' na gluasadan bodhaig a tha seo!
Boban enjoys the rhythm of the music on the radio so much, that he begins to dance. But Fuigheag isn’t sure what these movements are all about! Narrator - Kathleen MacInnes Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc:
Gach oidhche bidh Comhachag a’ cumail geàrd air a’ choille. Ge-tà, leis a’ ghealach a’ sìor fhàs tana agus a’ choille a’ sìor fhàs dorcha, tha Comhachag a’ fàs aonranach. Chan eil e idir cho measail air a dhleastanas. Gu fortanach, tha plàna aig Maigheach!
Every night, Owl keeps watch over the forest. But with the Moon growing thinner and the woods growing darker night by night, Owl begins to feel lonely. He starts to dread his duties. Luckily, Hare has a plan! Director - Linda MacLeod Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc:
Tha Mamaidh air rud dìomhair innse do Phompon - tha i air cuirm a' chur air dòigh 'son cò-là-breith Dadaidh - ach ciamar a chumas Pompon an rùn-dìomhair?
Mamaidh has told Pompon a secret - she's arranged a party for Daddy's birthday. But how will Pompon keep the secret? Pompon - Lana Beaton Rita - Mischa Macpherson Seòras - Calum MacKinnon Siùsaidh - Rebecca MacLennan Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc:
Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean air an dòigh glan nuair tha na duilleagan a’ cuachail gu talamh!
Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are delighted when the leaves start twirling to the ground! Ladybird - Emily Davidson Narrator/Bee - Rachel Kate Macleod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc:
‘S e latha ciùin a th’ ann, ach tha Nìp a’ cladhach thuill air feadh an eilein, is cha stad e. Tha Àtaidh is Tilidh a’ feuchainn ri obrachadh a-mach gu dè tha ga fhàgail air bhioran mar seo. Feumaidh gur e a cho-là-breith a th’ ann!
It is a peaceful day but Neep is digging holes all over the Island and won’t stop. Abney and Teal try to work out why he is so excited. It must be his birthday! Teal - Linda MacLeod Abney - Tony Kearney Producer - Linda MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Editor - Chas Chalmers Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc:

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc:
Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mòrag Anna NicNèill a’ leughadh Air a’ Chladach. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Anna Milbourne agus a dhealbhachadh le Erica-Jane Waters. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid.
A bedtime story for young children. Morag Ann MacNeil reads Air a’ Chladach by Anna Milbourne, illustrated by Erica-Jane Waters and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod. Presenter - Morag Ann MacNeil.

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc:
Tha Hilda, Flòraidh is Daibhidh a’ feuchainn ri bràistean Sgùdan Sporais às ùr a chosnadh. Air sgàth sin, tha 'ad dol a’ shireadh planntraisean annasach ionadail – agus abair g’ eil sin na chuairt-dànachd glè inntinneach.
Hilda, Flòraidh and Daibhidh are trying to earn new Sgùdan Sporrais badges. They go in search of rare, local plants, and this turns into a very interesting adventure. Hilda - Mischa Macpherson Mum - Anna Murray Daibhidh (David) - Ellen MacDonald Flòraidh (Frida) - Lauren Macdonald Victoria Van Gale - Kathleen MacInnes Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Stri
programme.desc:
Tha preasantairean CBBC ALBA uabhasach fhèin measail air dùbhlain ach saoil cò shoirbhicheas is Shanni a’ tadhal orra?
The CBBC ALBA presenters love a good challenge, but who will emerge victorious as Shanni joins them? Presenter - Calum MacDonald Presenter - Ellen Macdonald Executive Producer - Una MacDonald.

programme.title: Geamaichean Gorach
programme.desc:
Mar ‘s àbhaist, tha Coinneach Clogaid a’ feuchainn ri casg a chur air a h-uile Farpaiseach eile. Na can rium gu bheil e dol a bhuannachadh an trup-sa, ge-tà? ‘S cinnteach nach eil?
As ever, Coinneach Clogaid is trying to stop all the other competitors. Don’t tell me he’s going to win this time though. Surely not? Aithris - David Walker Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed.

programme.title: A-null ’s a-nall
programme.desc:
Tha Lena na nighean òg Roma agus, ged nach eil e àbhaisteach sa chultar aic’, ’s e a miann a bhith na ballerina. A dh’aindeoin a h-uile cnap-starra, tha i treun gu soirbheachadh.
Lena is a young Roma girl and, even though it's not normal practice in her culture, she dreams of being a ballerina. Despite all the obstacles, she is determined to succeed. Lena - Anna Graham Mum - Jo Macminn Mila - Iona Davidson Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec Macdonald.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc:
Abair gu bheil maorach a’ còrdadh ri na seòid agus anns a’ phrògram-sa, tha iad a’ còcaireachd le crùbag, rud air a bheilear tric a’ dèanamh dearmaid. Tha Ùisdean ag ullachadh ciad cùrsa dathte a’ cleachdadh feòil chrùbaig dhonn agus deiseag.
Tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh Linguine Crùbaig fhad ’s a tha Ùisdean cuideachd a’ dèanamh pasta, Ravioli air a lìonadh le feòil crùbaig agus bisque crùbaig. Aig deireadh gnothaich, tha Ruairidh a’ cruthachadh biadh sònraichte, spring rolls crùbaig teth is fuar.
The lads love seafood, and the often overlooked and under-rated crab features in this episode. Uisdean prepares a colourful crab starter using brown and velvet crab meat.
Ruaridh makes an interesting crab linguini while Uisdean continues the pasta thread by making Ravioli filled with crab meat and a crab bisque. To finish, Ruaridh creates a speciality, hot and cold crab spring rolls.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Uisdean Macleod Presenter - Roddy Munro Executive Producer - Ishbel Maclennan Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Producer - Kenneth Stewart.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.sub-title: Aig An Taigh ║ S2(A2)E5/13. At the House ║ S2(A2)E5/13
programme.desc:
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she introduces words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, home, work and communication.
We meet diligent learners who have embraced speaking Gaelic, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. And, the intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online at www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Executive Producer - Una MacDonald.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc:
Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA.
Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc:
Actress turned interior designer Erica Macpherson takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers she finds new ideas for designing old spaces.
Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Nic a’ Phersain, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Erica Macpherson Editor - Paul Duke Director - Calum Angus Mackay Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: Surfing: Marcachd an Tuinn/Riding the Wave
programme.desc:
Aig Geamannan Oilimpigeach 2024, tha an luchd-surfaidh as fheàrr san t-saoghal gu bhith a’ farpais 20,000 cileameatair air falbh bho Paris, ann an Tahiti. Tha tè aig a bheil ùidh mhòr ann an surfadh, Ceitlin Lilidh a’ toirt thugainn sreath de dhà phàirt air eachdraidh surfadh air feadh an t-saoghail. Do mhuinntir Tahiti, far an do thòisich surfadh bho thùs, tha e nas motha na spòrs, ’s e taisbeanadh a th’ ann de chultar mhuinntir an uisge, muinntir Pholinìsia.
Le tòrr de chultar agus eachdraidh bheairteach muinntir Pholinìsia cha mhòr air a sguabhadh air falbh, feumar taing a thoirt do leithid Tom Pōhaku Stone oir chaidh traidiseanan a bhith a’ dannsa air bùird fiodha a thoirt chun an ath ghinealaich agus chun an t-saoghail air fad, far a bheil a-nis, na deichean de mhilleanan dhaoine le ùidh ann an surfadh. Airson a’ chiad uair, tha àite aig surfadh aig na Geamannan Oilimpigeach.
Bho bhith na chur-seachad annasach do luchd-turais bhon Taobh an Iar a’ dol a Hawaii tràth anns an fhicheadamh linn gu bhith na phàirt mhòr de dhòigh-beatha na tràghad ann an California air taobh an iar Ameireagaidh. Cha tug e fada gus an do ràinig surfadh cladaichean fuar na h-Alba is dithis no triùir a’ cur aodach snàmh orra agus a’ dol a-mach air na bùird aca fhèin.
Bho stuadhan mòra Tahiti gu dùbhlain nan tonn sa gheamhradh ann an Inbhir Theòrsa agus tachartasan stuadhan mòra Nazaré ann am Portugal. ’S e sgeulachd de spioradalachd, spòrs, daoine ainmeil, fasan agus fealla-dhà a th’ ann an cuairt Ceitlin Lilidh ’s i ag ionnsachadh mu eachdraidh surfadh.
At the 2024 Olympic Games, the world's best surfers competed 20,000km from Paris, in Tahiti. Keen surfer Ceitlin Lilidh presents a series on the world history of surfing. Much more than a sport to the people of Tahiti where surfing was born, it is an expression of a culture, the people of the water, the Polynesians.
While much of the rich culture and history of the Polynesian people was almost wiped out, thanks to guardians like Tom Pōhaku Stone, the traditions of dancing on wooden boards was passed on to future generations and to the rest of the world where it is now practised by tens of millions of enthusiasts. Surfing has now for the first time earned its place at the Olympics.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.sub-title: Chan eil sgiobair ann coltach rium!/No one’s a better captain than me ║ Peicein/PetitS1E15/26
programme.desc:
Tha Peicein is Lòra ag argamaid mu dheidhinn cò aca a bu chòir na riaghailtean a dhèanamh suas airson geama Ghriogair is Raghnaill. Fhad ’s a tha iadsan a’ feuchainn ri obrachadh a-mach cò aca a bu chòir a bhith nan sgiobair, tha Griogair agus Raghnall a’ cumail a’ cluich às aonais a’ bhuill.
Petit and Laura argue about who should be the one that makes the rules of Greg and Roman's game. While they decide who should be the captain, Greg and Roman wait for them to make a decision and continue playing without the ball. programme.desc:
Tha rèis dhan bhàrr dol bhith ann – a’ chiad oileanach a chuireas flaga air Beinn Rocaid a' buinnig na duais. Ach bheil cuideigin na chealgaire?
A race to the summit is going to take place - the first student to plant a flag on Mount Rocket will win the trophy. But is somebody a cheat? programme.sub-title: A' Chiad Choinneamh – An Neach-teichidh (Pàirt 1) ║ S1E33/52

Bitzer has completed all his chores and is at a bit of a loss. He's delighted when he discovers the flock's barn needs a good tidy-up, until he comes across a wonky picture that just won't hang straight.

programme.title: Alba Eagalach
programme.desc:
Tha sgioba CBBC ALBA a’ toirt thugainn cuid de na sgeulachdan agus na tachartasan as eagalaiche ann an eachdraidh na h-Alba. Anns a’ phrògram seo, coinnichidh sinn ri Uilleam Uallas agus cluinnidh sinn mun bheatha eagalach a bh’ aige ach chan eil e fhèin ro dheònach bruidhinn mu dheidhinn!
CBBC ALBA brings us some of the scariest stories from Scottish history. In this episode, we meet William Wallace and uncover the grisly details of his life. Surprisingly, he doesn't seem too keen to talk about these!

programme.title: Flix
programme.sub-title: Burma : An Caraid as Fheàrr ║ S1E12/13
programme.desc:
Tha eadar-dhealaichidhean air an comharrachadh san sgoil is, mar dhùbhlain, tha aig Flix is Burma ri bhith càirdeil ri chèile. Chan eil fhios ciamar a dh'obraicheas seo a-mach ge-tà!
Differences are celebrated in school and, as a challenge, Flix and Burma have to be friendly with one another. Nobody knows how this will work out though! Flix - Derek MacIntosh Munchkin - Calum MacKinnon Burma - Kathleen MacInnes Tomaidh - Derek Murray Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec Macdonald.

programme.title: Fillte
programme.desc:
Fillte goes on a journey throughout Scotland to discover the history and contemporary hand-crafted practice behind the artisan production of woven fabrics, such as wool, hemp, linen, grasses, leather and many more unorthodox materials.
Tha Fillte a gabhail turas tro Alba a’ sireadh eachdraidh agus sgeulachdan an latha ’n diugh co-cheangailte ris an luchd-ciùird a tha snìomh ‘s ag obrachadh diofar stuthan, leithid, clòimh, corcach, anart, feur,leathar, agus iomadh seorsa stuth iongantach eile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tron tuilleadh cheumannan airson ar misneachadh gus leantainn oirnn a bhith bruidhinn na Gàidhlig. Thairis air an t-sreath seo, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin a’ chànan, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir tro chòmhraidhean goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr, cuid a bha fileanta agus a sguir ga cleachdadh agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba ’s e ann an diofar àitichean air feadh na dùthcha.Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she introduces words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy will support us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, home, work, communication and people skills.
We meet diligent speakers who have embraced the language, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. And, the intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Producer - Colin MacLeod Director - Sam Pearce Executive Producer - Una McDonald.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc:
Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA.
Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc:
Ramsay MacMahon meets well-known Gaels across Scotland to share stories, appreciate nature and reflect on their lives. Ramsay walks with Coinneach Rankin in Lochalsh, the area where he grew up and still calls home.
San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Tha Ramsay a’ coinneachadh ri Coinneach MacFhraing ann an Loch Aillse, an t-àite far an do thogar e agus ris an abair e fhathast a dhachaigh.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Ramsay MacMahon Series Producer - Robyn Low Editor - Mairead Morrison.

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.sub-title: Fhionnlainn agus an Ruis ║ S1E3/4. Finland & Russia ║ S1E3/4
programme.desc:
Tha Ramsay MacMahon ag ionnsachadh mu bheatha air a’ chrìoch eadar an Fhionnlainn agus an Ruis. Bho thug an Ruis ionnsaigh air an Ucràin ann an 2022 tha a’ chrìoch air dùnadh gu tur, ag atharrachadh beatha dhaoine air gach taobh. Anns an Fhionnlainn, cluinnidh Ramsay sgeulachdan bho theaghlaichean a chaidh a’ sgaradh bho an luchd-gràdh air taobh eile na crìche. Coinnichidh e riuthsan air a bheil an dleastanas ‘son tèarainteachd aig a’ chrìoch agus cluinnidh e bho dhaoine a chaill am beòshlaint’ gu h-obann air sgàth an dùnaidh.
Ramsay MacMahon learns about life along the border between Finland and Russia. Since Russia’s attack on Ukraine in 2022 the border has closed completely, transforming the lives of people on both sides. In Finland, Ramsay hears the stories of families who have been separated from their loved ones on the other side, meets those responsible for securing the border and hears from people who have lost their livelihood overnight because of its closure.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc:
Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh.
The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s-1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Narrator - Kirsty Macdonald Producer - Andy Mackinnon Production Manager - Eilidh Johnson Executive Producer - Margaret Cameron.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: Nirribhidh ║ Dàna. S4. AnRoinn-EòrpaE1/5. Stetind ║ Dàna. S4. AnRoinn-EòrpaE1/5
programme.desc:
A’ sireadh Dànachd anns an Roinn Eòrpa, tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ siubhal gu dùthaich nam beann iongantach – Nirribhidh. Còmhla ri a chompanach sreap, Calum Gibb, bidh Coinneach a’ dìreadh ‘Stetind’, stùc le eachdraidh bheairteach a tha air mac-meanmna luchd-sreap a ghlacadh airson còrr is ceud bliadhna.
Seeking adventure on a grand scale in Europe, Coinneach Rankin travels to the mountain paradise of Norway. Along with his climbing partner, Calum Gibb, Coinneach makes an ascent of Stetind, a peak with a storied past that has captured the imagination of mountaineers for well over a century.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Coinneach Rankin Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod Producer - Rowan Green.

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc:
Lean sgeulachdan teaghlaichean leanabain a rugadh ro thràth, agus na sgiobaidhean meidigeach a tha a’ coimhead às an dèidh, anns an t-sreath bhrosnachail làn-fhaireachdainn seo a bheir dhuinn sealladh farsaing air na daoine agus air an obair.
Air cùl dorsan Aonad Dlùth-chùram Leanabain Ospadal Mhàthraichean Oilthigh Chorcaigh ann an Èirinn, coinnichidh sinn ris na nursaichean, na dotairean agus na lannsairean fìor-adhartach a tha a’ dèanamh obair-lannsa do-chreidsinneach air naoidheanan a rugadh cho tràth ri còig seachdainean air fhichead, agus anns nach eil ach cuideam pacaid flùir.
Le caractaran brosnachail agus blàtha, chì sinn an dìcheall agus an gràdh a bheir an cothrom as fheàrr do leanabain a thàinig ro thràth, agus sinn a’ compàirteachadh anns an aoibhneas a tha an cois na ciad làithean aca san t-saoghal.
Follow the stories of families and medical teams looking after premature babies in an emotive and inspiring full-access series.
Go behind-the-scenes of the neo-natal unit at Cork University Maternity Hospital in Ireland and meet the nurses, doctors and pioneering surgeons performing incredible life-saving treatment on babies born as early as 25 weeks and weighing the same amount as a bag of flour.
With inspirational and heartwarming characters, witness the dedication and love put into giving babies born preterm the best chance possible, and share in the joy of their first days of life.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc:
Tha sgioba bata teasairginn Fraochy Bay a' dol a-sas ann an trèanadh agus a sùil ri de na dh'fhaodadh tighinn le blàthachadh na cruinne. Tha am bàrd Torcuil Fearchar deònach cobhair a dhèanamh oirre ach co a nith cobhair aire-san?
The Fraochy Bay lifeboat crew are having a training day. The scenario involves an icy adventure. Passing poet Torquil Farquhar is roped in to help and is well-versed in his role, but what about the lifeboat crew?

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc:
Roghainn bho oidhche mhòr duaisean Na Trads 2022. A nochd ceòl bho St Roch’s & Tayside Young Fiddlers.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.sub-title: Fuaim an Airgid – The Sound of Cash ║ S1E3/6
programme.desc:
After years of unhappiness, mill worker Mairead finally walks out of her decades-long marriage and into the arms of the person she loves - hotel owner Cairistiona. However, as the women agree to wait for the right time to tell Mairead’s husband Boyd they are together, little do they know there’s someone watching from the shadows.
Às dèidh bliadhnaichean de mhì-thoileachas, tha neach-obrach na muilne, Mairead, a’ fàgail an duine aice às dèidh bliadhnaichean fada pòsta airson a bhith còmhla ris an neach air a bheil gaol aice – Cairistìona, aig a bheil an taigh-òsta. Ach, ged a tha na boireannaich agaontachadh feitheamh gus innse dha Boyd, an duine aig Mairead, gu bheil iad còmhla – ‘s beag a dh’fhios a th’ aca gu bheil cuideigin ‘san dorchadas gan coimhead.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Seumas - Ewen MacKinnon Sileas - Erica Morrison Donald - Eoghan MacDonald Murdina - Emma MacLeod Cairistiona - Kathryn MacKay Boyd - David Walker Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Production Manager - Mairi MacKinnon.

programme.desc:

There’s a lot happening when Bing and friends make leaf pictures in the forest, but the wind doesn’t make things easy for them. Thig air turas eile sgoinneil le na h-Abadas. 'S e 'put' am facal ùr a tha aca. Cò a thèid air a thòrr an-diugh: Hari, Ela, neo Seren?
Join the Abadas for another 'abadobedee' adventure. This episode's word is 'buoy'. Who will be chosen to find today's exciting new word; Hari, Ela or Seren?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc:
‘S e latha ciùin a th’ ann, ach tha Nìp a’ cladhach thuill air feadh an eilein, is cha stad e. Tha Àtaidh is Tilidh a’ feuchainn ri obrachadh a-mach gu dè tha ga fhàgail air bhioran mar seo. Feumaidh gur e a cho-là-breith a th’ ann!
It is a peaceful day but Neep is digging holes all over the Island and won’t stop. Abney and Teal try to work out why he is so excited. It must be his birthday! programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc:
Tha an t-Iasg Garibaldi ag innse dhuinn mar a tha ìomhaigh aige ri chumail suas, mar a bhios e a' lorg a charaid, agus mar a bhios e a’ coimhead às deidh nead làn uighean
The Garibaldi Fish tells us how he has an image to uphold, the way he finds his mate and how he looks after a nest full of eggs. Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc:
Nuair tha Bonns is Uilidh a' sàbhaladh Throig bhon Bhògais-shìd’, tha e uabhasach neo-thaingeil. Cho neo-thaingeil ‘s gu bheil e a' tilleadh air ais chun na Bògaisean. Ach tha e ag ionnsachadh gu bheil caraidean feumail aig a' cheann thall!
When Bonns and Uilidh save Troig from Bògais-shìd’, he is very ungrateful. So much so, that he returns to see the Bògaisean. However, he learns that friends are helpful, at the end of the day! programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc:

Uilidh wants to prove that he is a hero just like the Un-named Gumbal. How will he get on? Is he brave or is he just foolish? programme.desc:

programme.desc:
Tha Hilda, Flòraidh is Daibhidh a’ feuchainn ri bràistean Sgùdan Sporais às ùr a chosnadh. Air sgàth sin, tha 'ad dol a’ shireadh planntraisean annasach ionadail – agus abair g’ eil sin na chuairt-dànachd glè inntinneach.
Hilda, Flòraidh and Daibhidh are trying to earn new Sgùdan Sporrais badges. They go in search of rare, local plants, and this turns into a very interesting adventure. Hilda - Mischa Macpherson Mum - Anna Murray Daibhidh (David) - Ellen MacDonald Flòraidh (Frida) - Lauren Macdonald Victoria Van Gale - Kathleen MacInnes Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc:
Abair gu bheil maorach a’ còrdadh ri na seòid agus anns a’ phrògram-sa, tha iad a’ còcaireachd le crùbag, rud air a bheilear tric a’ dèanamh dearmaid. Tha Ùisdean ag ullachadh ciad cùrsa dathte a’ cleachdadh feòil chrùbaig dhonn agus deiseag.
Tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh Linguine Crùbaig fhad ’s a tha Ùisdean cuideachd a’ dèanamh pasta, Ravioli air a lìonadh le feòil crùbaig agus bisque crùbaig. Aig deireadh gnothaich, tha Ruairidh a’ cruthachadh biadh sònraichte, spring rolls crùbaig teth is fuar.
The lads love seafood, and the often overlooked and under-rated crab features in this episode. Uisdean prepares a colourful crab starter using brown and velvet crab meat.
Ruaridh makes an interesting crab linguini while Uisdean continues the pasta thread by making Ravioli filled with crab meat and a crab bisque. To finish, Ruaridh creates a speciality, hot and cold crab spring rolls.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Uisdean Macleod Presenter - Roddy Munro Executive Producer - Ishbel Maclennan Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Producer - Kenneth Stewart.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leantainn oirre ’s i gar toirt tro cheumannan a bharrachd ann a bhith ag ionnsachadh na Gàidhlig. Bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean làitheil agus, mar thè a dh’ionnsaich na Gàidhlig i fhèin, bheir Joy mìneachadh dhuinn air briathrachas, gràmar is gnathasan-cainnte ann an dòigh a tha furasta a thuigsinn.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh a th’ air Gàidhlig ionnsachadh gu àrd ìre neo a thogadh leis a’ Ghàidhlig air falbh bho sgìrean traidiseanta na Gàidhealtachd, agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh dhuinn air annasan is cuspairean ’s e air chuairt air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot, ann am pod-chraolaidhean SpeakGaelic air BBC Sounds agus tha na prògraman air fad rin lorg le fo-thiotalan air sianal YouTube SpeakGaelic.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to keep on speaking Gaelic. As in previous series, she introduces and explains usage for words and phrases on everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through vocabulary, grammar and idiom on topics such as medicine, politics, community and exercise.
Diligent speakers who have embraced the language join in, and the intrepid Calum Maclean ventures to forgotten corners of Scotland seeking hidden treasures.

It is increasingly popular with tourists, who arrive by train, bus or under sail - a destination offering exceptional seafood and a traditional holiday experience for the many thousands of visitors to enjoy. programme.title: An t-Uisge/Rain Stories
programme.sub-title: A' Tuigsinn An Uisge/Understanding Rain ║ Ant-Uisge/RainStoriesS1E1/3
programme.desc:
Tha buaidh air a bhith aig uisge air cultaran agus traidiseanan bho riamh. Bidh luchd-saidheans ga rannsachadh, bidh coimhearsnachdan ag ùrnaigh air a shon, agus bidh riaghaltasan a’ feuchainn ri smachd a ghabhail air.
Ach dè th’ ann an uisge agus carson a tha e nas cudromaiche a-nis na bha e a-riamh? Tha Anne Lundon a’ lìbhrigeadh an t-sreath ùr, fiosrachail seo a’ rannsachadh an t-saidheans agus na sgeulachdan air cùlaibh an nì a tha a’ beathachadh dhaoine.
Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha sinn a’ tadhal air Uamhan na Stuaidh Marbhail. Tha fiosrachadh ri lorg mun ghnàth-shìde thràth anns an àrainneachd seo, air an tug an t-uisge buaidh mhòr, agus a tha trì cheud ’s ceathrad millean bliadhna a dh’ aois.
Bidh Anne a’ cluinntinn mu uisge searbhagach a chaidh aithneachadh an dèidh An Tionndadh Gnìomhachais. Agus bidh i a’ tadhal air làrach rannsachaidh faisg air Dùn Èideann, far am bi luchd-saidheans a’ cumail sùil air truailleadh Nitrogen san uisge againn san là an-diugh.
Anns na ceathradan, bhiotar a’ sìolachadh nan sgòthan gus cumhachd dhroch stoirmean a lùghdachadh agus an uairsin ann am miseanan dìomhair an airm aig àm Cogadh Bhietnam. Tha Anne a’ siubhal gu Abu Dhabi far am bi i a’ coinneachadh ris an fheadhainn a tha air thoiseach air chàich ann a bhith a’ cruthachadh uisge san là an-diugh.
Rain has influenced our cultures and traditions since time began. Scientists study it, communities pray for it and governments try to control it. But what is rain and why is it more important now than ever? Anne Lundon presents this revealing series exploring the science and stories behind this life-giving force.
We descend into Ireland’s Marble Arch Caves, a 340 million-year-old environment shaped by rain, which has clues to our early climate. Anne hears about acid rain, first identified after the Industrial Revolution, and visits a research site near Edinburgh where scientists monitor nitrogen pollution in our rain today.
Cloud-seeding was used in the 1940s in attempts to reduce the power of hurricanes and later in top secret US military missions during the Vietnam War. Anne travels to Abu Dhabi where she meets some of those at the forefront of the technique today - literally making rain.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc:

As dèidh 95 bliadhna de dh'eachdraidh phròiseil chaidh innse gun robh Cluba Lùth-chleasachd Third Lanark banc-briste, agus chaidh na geataichean gu Pàirce Chathkin an dùnadh airson an turas mu dheireadh.
Tha Third Lanark ag innse an sgeulachd mu dheidhinn cluba coimhearsnachd sònraichte, a' coimhead ri mar a chaidh a stèidheachadh, na làithean buidhe a thuilleadh air na làithean a bu dhuirche an uair a chaidh an cluba à bith.
In 1967, as it edged towards its centenary, a much-loved social and cultural institution was consigned to history. Following 95 years of emotional highs and lows, Glasgow's Third Lanark Athletic Club was bankrupt, and the gates to Cathkin Park were closed.
Third Lanark is the fascinating story of this iconic community club, exploring its formation and existence, as well as its catastrophic collapse. Narrator - Alex O'Henley Executive Producer - Margot McCuaig Executive Producer - Iseabail Mactaggart.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
International Men’s Day was established in 1999 to highlight positive male role models and raise awareness of men’s health and wellbeing. Ahead of this year’s event, Sean Fletcher is in Leeds exploring what it means to be a man in modern society, and how faith, friendship and a sense of purpose can help men thrive in mind, body and spirit.
He meets rugby league legend Jamie Jones-Buchanan, now CEO of Leeds Rhinos, where he made 421 appearances, as well as representing England and Great Britain. Jamie reflects on growing up without a father figure in one of the UK’s most deprived areas, and how rugby and his Christian faith provided positive male role models, and a sense of belonging and purpose. He challenges stereotypes of the macho rugby player, and his passion for helping the next generation comes to life during a training session.
In the Welsh valleys, Pastor John Funnell reflects on the extraordinary number of young men joining his congregation. John left a highly paid career after becoming a Christian and moved to one of Europe’s most deprived communities. He explains how his church offers practical skills, mentoring, friendship and faith, helping men see that their past does not have to determine their future.
Back in Leeds, Sean meets Chris Sayburn, a minister and renowned worship leader who spent 12 years living with chronic pain following complications after spinal surgery. He tells Sean how exercise and faith have helped him rebuild his life and how a community of men became a lifeline.
With uplifting hymns and songs from around the UK.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The open ocean is the largest wilderness on earth. Covering more than half of the planet's surface, it appears at first glance to be an endless blue desert. Yet hidden here are some of the most extraordinary animals.
We uncover the surprising strategies, epic journeys and remarkable resilience that allows life to thrive here. From wandering predators and drifting castaways to giant whales and tiny turtle hatchlings, it is a world where life survives against the odds.
The journey begins far beyond the sight of land, where California sea lions travel miles into the Pacific in search of seasonal, rich fishing grounds. Here, they join one of the open ocean's great feeding spectacles as black skipjack tuna, mahi-mahi and seabirds converge on vast schools of fish in a dramatic battle for a meal.
Some animals aren’t just visitors here; they spend their entire lives in this immense expanse. Rough-toothed dolphins have roamed the oceans since before woolly mammoths walked the earth, and yet we know very little about them. To help find food, they use sophisticated teamwork and ingenious hunting techniques that have rarely been witnessed.
Although the open ocean seems like a featureless expanse, it is shaped by powerful currents that flow across the globe like invisible rivers. These currents transport animals, nutrients and entire ecosystems across immense distances. For ocean drifters such as Smith's swimming crabs, the currents are both a lifeline and a gamble, carrying them through a world where danger can appear without warning.
Currents also drive one of the largest floating ecosystems on the planet. Today, the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt stretches over 5,000 miles across the ocean. But changing conditions are sweeping unprecedented amounts of this seaweed onto coastlines throughout the Caribbean. On the beaches of Mexico, turtle hatchlings emerging from their nests face a daunting new obstacle as mountains of sargassum block their path to the sea. Their struggle reveals how changes in the open ocean can have profound consequences far beyond the horizon.
In the Pacific, we follow one of nature's greatest aerial pirates, a frigatebird mother raising her chick alone.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

programme.sub-title: Perthshire - Rebuilding an Ancient Settlement ║ S1

In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Will and Dom are in Aberfeldy’s Crannog Centre, where visitors experience recreations of 5,000-year-old traditional dwellings. After a devastating fire three years ago put the project in jeopardy, thatcher Scott is looking to the future and building a new cookhouse, using traditional techniques and local materials. It could mean big business for the centre and increased opportunities to work with the local community, but creating Iron Age dwellings in the modern age is anything but simple.
Will then heads off to Scone Palace, crowning place of Scottish kings, to meet a couple with a family heirloom in need of rescue. It’s a handwritten Gaelic piping music book, handed down from Ian’s great-grandfather Donald, known as the Hero of Alma after his actions in the Crimean War. Now severely damaged, the music in its brittle pages might be lost forever if bookbinder Chris Shaw cannot bring it back from the brink. Ian will never play the songs it contains, as he has been battling motor neurone disease for the past decade, but he hopes if Chris Shaw is successful, the book can be passed down to his own son, also named Donald in honour of his ancestor.
Always in search of a new challenge, Dom joins a Perth-based family business whose handmade sporrans are the perfect accessory to Scotland’s famous kilts. It’s a critically endangered heritage craft that dates back to the 12th century, and the family is turning to technology to keep up with the challenge faced by cheaper, mass-produced versions made abroad. Dom is always eager to get on the tools, so what will his hosts make of his attempts at leatherworking? programme.title: Young, British and Tradwife
programme.desc:
Tradwives are trending. The term is in the dictionary, and the hashtag has over 300 million views on TikTok. Online tradwives promote the pleasures of domesticity and teach others how to be perfect homemakers in effortless and elegant social media videos that generate millions of likes. But they are not just an online phenomenon. Women in the real world, inspired by online influencers, are increasingly rejecting feminism, workplace hustle and hook-up culture to bake sourdough, homeschool the kids and obey their husbands.
BAFTA- and Grierson Award-nominated documentarian Poppy Jay wants to know why the tradwife world of domestic chores and submission appeals to so many. Reflecting on her own experience of forced marriage, she packs away her camera, pins on an apron and meets with British tradwives to find out if this is what true choice looks like in the 21st century.
As she juggles baking, sewing and schooling, she asks if a movement that demands submission to a husband is the solution to modern burnout or just the latest manifestation of an age-old misogynistic culture shaped by men, for men.
Poppy meets women from across the tradwife spectrum, from the newly married coach of ‘biblical wifery’ with 70,000 TikTok followers to the homeschooling mother of seven, to discover why the simple life rooted in traditional Christian values is suddenly so popular. Immersing herself in family life, Poppy challenges her own preconceptions, asking why any women would choose to submit to her husband and whether feminism has, as the tradwives claim, betrayed women by promising them they can have it all. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Ayrshire - Restoring Robert Burns Graffiti ║ S1
programme.desc:
Carpenter Will and horologist Steve are far from home today, exploring Ayrshire on Scotland’s west coast. Their first stop is the Scottish Boat Building School in Irvine, where Tom is waiting with a very unusual vessel. It’s a three-piece canoe designed in the 1930s and small enough to fit in the guard’s van of a train, which meant tourists could bring their own canoes on holiday in the years before owning a car was commonplace. It represents a different kind of freedom for Tom, though. His achondroplasia means a regular-size canoe is too difficult to manoeuvre. If this folding version can be fixed, he will finally have the freedom to take his daughter out exploring the waterways of Britain.
Ayrshire is the birthplace of Scotland’s national poet, Robert Burns, and many of the towns and villages in the region can boast strong links to his life and works. So it’s no surprise that when Will is called to Barr Castle in Galston, he comes face-to-face with a very special artefact. It’s a windowpane with a hand inscription by Robert Burns himself. However, it has suffered some damage in the past, so for decades its current custodians have had it hidden away in a cupboard for safekeeping. With the help of ceramics expert Kirsten Ramsay, they hope to once again put it on display. Fixing glass is notoriously difficult, and Kirsten definitely feels the pressure of getting such an important object looking back to its best.
While in the area, Steve takes the chance to visit Kays in Mauchline, who have been crafting curling stones for over 170 years. Using a dense granite quarried from a single Scottish island, these dedicated craftspeople hone stones of unparalleled quality for use in the Winter Olympics. Steve gets the chance to help with the process, but will it be gold, silver or bronze for his efforts? Five chefs remain in the race for a place in the quarter-final. But two more high-pressure challenges, which will test every aspect of their cooking, stand in their way.
Marcus and Monica are joined by special guest Adejoké Bakare, whose restaurant Chishuru is at the forefront of West African fine dining. With no recipe to follow, they’ll have to rely entirely on their palates, instincts and technical skills to recreate Adejoké’s dish. programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc:
The BBC’s biggest comedy talent search has reached its final night. Almost 1,000 comedians applied to this year’s New Comedy Awards. More than 100 went head-to-head at showcases across the country, and just 30 made it through to the knockout heats. Now only six remain.
The finalists take to the stage one last time, each hoping to win over the judges and be crowned BBC New Comedian 2026.
The grand final is filmed in front of a full house at Birmingham’s iconic Town Hall. Presenting the night is award-winning writer, comedian and Hollywood actor Guz Khan, who made the journey from stand-up to the screen and knows exactly what the night means to the acts waiting in the wings.
Leading the judging panel is the multitalented and multi-award-winning comedian, actor and writer Amy Gledhill. Joining her are Kiell Smith-Bynoe, star of Ghosts and Taskmaster, and Dan Tiernan, a former BBC New Comedy Awards winner. Together, they weigh up the writing, the delivery and the originality of every act before choosing their winner.
Rounding off the night is a very special performance from last year’s winner, Eli Hart, who returns to hand over the award to this year’s champion.
The winner will receive a paid commission to write and perform their own 30-minute audio pilot under the mentorship of a BBC comedy commissioner, plus a trophy and £1,000 in cash. For a comic at the start of their career, it is a rare opportunity that could open plenty of doors.

Will David Burville be able to get this family heirloom - handed down from Carole’s great-aunt Elsie - making music on the high seas again?

Now producing more than 1,400 shinty sticks each year from his Highland workshop, Alan instructs Will in the intricacies of creating equipment to stand up to the rigors of this hard-fought game. The four chefs who have survived the intensity of the heats are back in the kitchen. Now they must prove to Marcus and Monica that they have the consistency, confidence and creativity to take on the next level of the competition.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
International Men’s Day was established in 1999 to highlight positive male role models and raise awareness of men’s health and wellbeing. Ahead of this year’s event, Sean Fletcher is in Leeds exploring what it means to be a man in modern society, and how faith, friendship and a sense of purpose can help men thrive in mind, body and spirit.
He meets rugby league legend Jamie Jones-Buchanan, now CEO of Leeds Rhinos, where he made 421 appearances, as well as representing England and Great Britain. Jamie reflects on growing up without a father figure in one of the UK’s most deprived areas, and how rugby and his Christian faith provided positive male role models, and a sense of belonging and purpose. He challenges stereotypes of the macho rugby player, and his passion for helping the next generation comes to life during a training session.
In the Welsh valleys, Pastor John Funnell reflects on the extraordinary number of young men joining his congregation. John left a highly paid career after becoming a Christian and moved to one of Europe’s most deprived communities. He explains how his church offers practical skills, mentoring, friendship and faith, helping men see that their past does not have to determine their future.
Back in Leeds, Sean meets Chris Sayburn, a minister and renowned worship leader who spent 12 years living with chronic pain following complications after spinal surgery. He tells Sean how exercise and faith have helped him rebuild his life and how a community of men became a lifeline.
With uplifting hymns and songs from around the UK.
1. Sweet Heart of Jesus - Leeds Cathedral 2. Amazing Grace - The Kingdom Choir 3. Facing a Task Unfinished - Lisburn Cathedral 4. Lord of All Hopefulness - Chris Sayburn and Friends 5. programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The open ocean is the largest wilderness on earth. Covering more than half of the planet's surface, it appears at first glance to be an endless blue desert. Yet hidden here are some of the most extraordinary animals.
We uncover the surprising strategies, epic journeys and remarkable resilience that allows life to thrive here. From wandering predators and drifting castaways to giant whales and tiny turtle hatchlings, it is a world where life survives against the odds.
The journey begins far beyond the sight of land, where California sea lions travel miles into the Pacific in search of seasonal, rich fishing grounds. Here, they join one of the open ocean's great feeding spectacles as black skipjack tuna, mahi-mahi and seabirds converge on vast schools of fish in a dramatic battle for a meal.
Some animals aren’t just visitors here; they spend their entire lives in this immense expanse. Rough-toothed dolphins have roamed the oceans since before woolly mammoths walked the earth, and yet we know very little about them. To help find food, they use sophisticated teamwork and ingenious hunting techniques that have rarely been witnessed.
Although the open ocean seems like a featureless expanse, it is shaped by powerful currents that flow across the globe like invisible rivers. These currents transport animals, nutrients and entire ecosystems across immense distances. For ocean drifters such as Smith's swimming crabs, the currents are both a lifeline and a gamble, carrying them through a world where danger can appear without warning.
Currents also drive one of the largest floating ecosystems on the planet. Today, the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt stretches over 5,000 miles across the ocean. But changing conditions are sweeping unprecedented amounts of this seaweed onto coastlines throughout the Caribbean. On the beaches of Mexico, turtle hatchlings emerging from their nests face a daunting new obstacle as mountains of sargassum block their path to the sea. Their struggle reveals how changes in the open ocean can have profound consequences far beyond the horizon.
In the Pacific, we follow one of nature's greatest aerial pirates, a frigatebird mother raising her chick alone.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The oceans have seasons just as the land does. Stretching across the temperate bands located between the freezing poles and the warm tropics lie the seasonal seas. Life is tough in these constantly changing waters, but if animals can persevere and adapt to change, there are myriad opportunities to not only survive but thrive here.
Winter in the seasonal seas is a battlefield. Storms whip up immense waves that can travel for thousands of miles, building to 30 metres in height before making landfall. On the Pacific coast of South America, such waves impact the lives of South America sea lions that have lived on this exposed coast for generations. Newborn pups and mothers are restricted to the colony, but the most intrepid males take a risk, leaving the tempestuous coast for unfamiliar waters and unusual prey - black-necked swans.
Some choose to escape, whilst others are undeterred by winters icy grip on the seasonal seas. In Patagonia, a female southern right whale arrives in the protected bay where she was likely born, in search of a mate. Testing prospective partners before accepting the best mate, she is rewarded with a gentle belly rub and embrace - a valuable pairing given that these animals were hunted to near extinction in the last century. The whaling ban increased this population from just 300 to 25,000, with a surprising twist – white calves.
As daylight lengthens and spring approaches, the greening of the seasonal seas commences. Plankton multiplies, creating huge blooms and feeding many species, including a rather peculiar crustacean, a porcelain crab. In the waters off Chile, over 200 million feast on this bounty, forming the largest-known aggregation of crabs in our oceans. But with limited space and an increased flow of plankton, the crabs do something remarkable - they organise themselves into structured lines, a behaviour that has never been filmed before.
As forests flourish on land, they also do so in the water. In spring, kelp, one of the fastest-growing organisms on earth, can lengthen by half a metre a day, forming submarine jungles that are home to a variety of creatures. In Japan, these lush fronds conceal a rarely seen fish, an eelpout, with a length of just ten centimetres.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Perthshire - Rebuilding an Ancient Settlement ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Will and Dom are in Aberfeldy’s Crannog Centre, where visitors experience recreations of 5,000-year-old traditional dwellings. After a devastating fire three years ago put the project in jeopardy, thatcher Scott is looking to the future and building a new cookhouse, using traditional techniques and local materials. It could mean big business for the centre and increased opportunities to work with the local community, but creating Iron Age dwellings in the modern age is anything but simple.
Will then heads off to Scone Palace, crowning place of Scottish kings, to meet a couple with a family heirloom in need of rescue. It’s a handwritten Gaelic piping music book, handed down from Ian’s great-grandfather Donald, known as the Hero of Alma after his actions in the Crimean War. Now severely damaged, the music in its brittle pages might be lost forever if bookbinder Chris Shaw cannot bring it back from the brink. Ian will never play the songs it contains, as he has been battling motor neurone disease for the past decade, but he hopes if Chris Shaw is successful, the book can be passed down to his own son, also named Donald in honour of his ancestor.
Always in search of a new challenge, Dom joins a Perth-based family business whose handmade sporrans are the perfect accessory to Scotland’s famous kilts. It’s a critically endangered heritage craft that dates back to the 12th century, and the family is turning to technology to keep up with the challenge faced by cheaper, mass-produced versions made abroad. Dom is always eager to get on the tools, so what will his hosts make of his attempts at leatherworking? programme.title: Young, British and Tradwife
programme.desc:
Tradwives are trending. The term is in the dictionary, and the hashtag has over 300 million views on TikTok. Online tradwives promote the pleasures of domesticity and teach others how to be perfect homemakers in effortless and elegant social media videos that generate millions of likes. But they are not just an online phenomenon. Women in the real world, inspired by online influencers, are increasingly rejecting feminism, workplace hustle and hook-up culture to bake sourdough, homeschool the kids and obey their husbands.
BAFTA- and Grierson Award-nominated documentarian Poppy Jay wants to know why the tradwife world of domestic chores and submission appeals to so many. Reflecting on her own experience of forced marriage, she packs away her camera, pins on an apron and meets with British tradwives to find out if this is what true choice looks like in the 21st century.
As she juggles baking, sewing and schooling, she asks if a movement that demands submission to a husband is the solution to modern burnout or just the latest manifestation of an age-old misogynistic culture shaped by men, for men.
Poppy meets women from across the tradwife spectrum, from the newly married coach of ‘biblical wifery’ with 70,000 TikTok followers to the homeschooling mother of seven, to discover why the simple life rooted in traditional Christian values is suddenly so popular. Immersing herself in family life, Poppy challenges her own preconceptions, asking why any women would choose to submit to her husband and whether feminism has, as the tradwives claim, betrayed women by promising them they can have it all. programme.sub-title: Devon - Emergency Surgery for Daisy the Cow ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Will and Dom travel to Devon, and where better to find Daisy, the oversized fibreglass dairy cow lantern? She’s been a fixture at Hemyock Light Parade for a decade, but time hasn’t been kind to their bovine mascot. She’s lost an ear, a couple of hooves, and her body is dirty and cracked. It’s going to take some lateral thinking, and the skills of some exciting new experts, if she’s to take her place at the head of the parade once again.
In Poole, Will meets Ronnie, who has a musical instrument that reached the peak of its popularity in the 1920s and 1930s and which he would like fixed. It’s a banjolele that his father, part of the Windrush generation, brought from Jamaica to England. Most famously associated with George Formby, Ronnie’s mixture of banjo and ukulele is struggling to play a tune now, suffering from damage to the frets and a loose drum head. They’ll need to be fixed before luthier Julyan can even think about starting the cosmetic work required to the veneer.
Dom checks in on an old friend in Torquay. He’s at Dave Smith’s workshop, overlooking the harbour, to try his hand at the lost art of brilliant cutting before turning a newly decorated piece of glass into a Victorian-style mirror. As Dave can boast clients like David Beckham, John Meyer and Disney, it’s a rare chance for Dom to get some tips straight from a master craftsman. Fish and chips by the sea are an added bonus. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Ayrshire - Restoring Robert Burns Graffiti ║ S1
programme.desc:
Carpenter Will and horologist Steve are far from home today, exploring Ayrshire on Scotland’s west coast. Their first stop is the Scottish Boat Building School in Irvine, where Tom is waiting with a very unusual vessel. It’s a three-piece canoe designed in the 1930s and small enough to fit in the guard’s van of a train, which meant tourists could bring their own canoes on holiday in the years before owning a car was commonplace. It represents a different kind of freedom for Tom, though. His achondroplasia means a regular-size canoe is too difficult to manoeuvre. If this folding version can be fixed, he will finally have the freedom to take his daughter out exploring the waterways of Britain.
Ayrshire is the birthplace of Scotland’s national poet, Robert Burns, and many of the towns and villages in the region can boast strong links to his life and works. So it’s no surprise that when Will is called to Barr Castle in Galston, he comes face-to-face with a very special artefact. It’s a windowpane with a hand inscription by Robert Burns himself. However, it has suffered some damage in the past, so for decades its current custodians have had it hidden away in a cupboard for safekeeping. With the help of ceramics expert Kirsten Ramsay, they hope to once again put it on display. Fixing glass is notoriously difficult, and Kirsten definitely feels the pressure of getting such an important object looking back to its best.
While in the area, Steve takes the chance to visit Kays in Mauchline, who have been crafting curling stones for over 170 years. Using a dense granite quarried from a single Scottish island, these dedicated craftspeople hone stones of unparalleled quality for use in the Winter Olympics. Steve gets the chance to help with the process, but will it be gold, silver or bronze for his efforts? programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc:
The BBC’s biggest comedy talent search has reached its final night. Almost 1,000 comedians applied to this year’s New Comedy Awards. More than 100 went head-to-head at showcases across the country, and just 30 made it through to the knockout heats. Now only six remain.
The finalists take to the stage one last time, each hoping to win over the judges and be crowned BBC New Comedian 2026.
The grand final is filmed in front of a full house at Birmingham’s iconic Town Hall. Presenting the night is award-winning writer, comedian and Hollywood actor Guz Khan, who made the journey from stand-up to the screen and knows exactly what the night means to the acts waiting in the wings.
Leading the judging panel is the multitalented and multi-award-winning comedian, actor and writer Amy Gledhill. Joining her are Kiell Smith-Bynoe, star of Ghosts and Taskmaster, and Dan Tiernan, a former BBC New Comedy Awards winner. Together, they weigh up the writing, the delivery and the originality of every act before choosing their winner.
Rounding off the night is a very special performance from last year’s winner, Eli Hart, who returns to hand over the award to this year’s champion.
The winner will receive a paid commission to write and perform their own 30-minute audio pilot under the mentorship of a BBC comedy commissioner, plus a trophy and £1,000 in cash. For a comic at the start of their career, it is a rare opportunity that could open plenty of doors.
Now in their 30th year, the New Comedy Awards have helped launch the careers of comedy greats who regularly feature on our stages and screens, including Peter Kay, Lee Mack, Russell Howard, Romesh Ranganathan, Alan Carr, Sarah Millican, Josie Long and Joe Lycett.
The finalists are hoping to follow in their footsteps.
Six comics. One stage. One title. Who will be crowned BBC New Comedian 2026? programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
International Men’s Day was established in 1999 to highlight positive male role models and raise awareness of men’s health and wellbeing. Ahead of this year’s event, Sean Fletcher is in Leeds exploring what it means to be a man in modern society, and how faith, friendship and a sense of purpose can help men thrive in mind, body and spirit.
He meets rugby league legend Jamie Jones-Buchanan, now CEO of Leeds Rhinos, where he made 421 appearances, as well as representing England and Great Britain. Jamie reflects on growing up without a father figure in one of the UK’s most deprived areas, and how rugby and his Christian faith provided positive male role models, and a sense of belonging and purpose. He challenges stereotypes of the macho rugby player, and his passion for helping the next generation comes to life during a training session.
In the Welsh valleys, Pastor John Funnell reflects on the extraordinary number of young men joining his congregation. John left a highly paid career after becoming a Christian and moved to one of Europe’s most deprived communities. He explains how his church offers practical skills, mentoring, friendship and faith, helping men see that their past does not have to determine their future.
Back in Leeds, Sean meets Chris Sayburn, a minister and renowned worship leader who spent 12 years living with chronic pain following complications after spinal surgery. He tells Sean how exercise and faith have helped him rebuild his life and how a community of men became a lifeline.
With uplifting hymns and songs from around the UK.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
The open ocean is the largest wilderness on earth. Covering more than half of the planet's surface, it appears at first glance to be an endless blue desert. Yet hidden here are some of the most extraordinary animals.
We uncover the surprising strategies, epic journeys and remarkable resilience that allows life to thrive here. From wandering predators and drifting castaways to giant whales and tiny turtle hatchlings, it is a world where life survives against the odds.
The journey begins far beyond the sight of land, where California sea lions travel miles into the Pacific in search of seasonal, rich fishing grounds. Here, they join one of the open ocean's great feeding spectacles as black skipjack tuna, mahi-mahi and seabirds converge on vast schools of fish in a dramatic battle for a meal.
Some animals aren’t just visitors here; they spend their entire lives in this immense expanse. Rough-toothed dolphins have roamed the oceans since before woolly mammoths walked the earth, and yet we know very little about them. To help find food, they use sophisticated teamwork and ingenious hunting techniques that have rarely been witnessed.
Although the open ocean seems like a featureless expanse, it is shaped by powerful currents that flow across the globe like invisible rivers. These currents transport animals, nutrients and entire ecosystems across immense distances. For ocean drifters such as Smith's swimming crabs, the currents are both a lifeline and a gamble, carrying them through a world where danger can appear without warning.
Currents also drive one of the largest floating ecosystems on the planet. Today, the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt stretches over 5,000 miles across the ocean. But changing conditions are sweeping unprecedented amounts of this seaweed onto coastlines throughout the Caribbean. On the beaches of Mexico, turtle hatchlings emerging from their nests face a daunting new obstacle as mountains of sargassum block their path to the sea. Their struggle reveals how changes in the open ocean can have profound consequences far beyond the horizon.
In the Pacific, we follow one of nature's greatest aerial pirates, a frigatebird mother raising her chick alone.
